A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SportsTime/CoTR work, and all supplied pages, figures, tables and equations are readable. However, both refer to appendices covering implementation, release and scoring details that neither supplied PDF contains. The main papers support reliable comparison; appendix-level changes remain unavailable.

before.justification: v1 reports original SportsTime evaluations, CoTR experiments, component and frame-budget ablations, human assessments and judge-agreement analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised numerical results in several tables and figures.

M1.justification: The documented CoTR procedure retains timestamp overlays, temporal-reward GRPO and anchor-triggered local observation and verification. Section 4.2 renames Timestamp-Overlay Preprocessing to Visual Time Anchoring without changing its operation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SportsTime coverage: 1,575 videos and 14,326 QA pairs across five sports and five task types. The additional evaluated benchmarks remain LVBench, MLVU and VideoMME; no new domain or task coverage is reported.

E2.justification: Table 4 supplies an InternVL2.5-4B comparison on LVBench, replacing an asterisk with 40.8%, while retaining the other comparators. Table 2 changes VideoLLaMA-7B to VideoLLaMA3-7B with the same citation and scores; that label change alone does not establish a separate model evaluation.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes GLM-4.6v-Flash-9B's reported input budget from 512 to 640 frames while retaining its scores. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that the experiment was rerun. CoTR's training/inference frame budgets and the reported human-evaluation sample and rater counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7(a) revises the frame-budget sensitivity evidence at the existing budgets. In particular, Video-R1 now falls below VideoLLaMA at 96 and 192 frames, reversing their earlier ordering. The component ablations, video-length analysis and judge-reliability studies are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same judge-agreement statistics, human-rating distributions and Figure 7(b) variability display. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are newly reported. The added explanation of Figure 6's existing dots and mean bars clarifies presentation rather than changing statistical practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises full-CoTR Perception/Temporal/Tactical/Causal/Counterfactual scores from 25.12/14.93/34.56/26.12/40.21 to 26.42/15.43/34.55/27.21/42.22, and its average from 29.23 to 29.24. Tables 5-6 reflect corresponding updates; Table 4 fills the missing LVBench score, and Figure 7(a) changes several plotted results. Reporting corrections include the human-evaluation gain from 4.50 to 6.00 points, mIoU prose from 0.78 to 0.58 matching the unchanged 0.5812 table value, and Figure 6(b)'s ICR/FLC labels matching the existing prose.

T1.justification: The mathematical content present in both PDFs retains the same trajectory factorization, reward decomposition and Figure 5 reward formulas. Equation 3 merely makes trajectory dependence explicit. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added to the supplied text.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SportsTime with step-wise temporal evidence, CoTR combining grounded training and inference, and improved reasoning and grounding over baselines. Rewording does not materially alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 shifts its interpretation of full-CoTR gains from Temporal/Causal evidence linkage toward Perception/Causal improvements in identifying and integrating evidence. It also characterizes transfer more cautiously as promising transferability and changes the human FLC assessment from highest to high, avoiding an unsupported comparative characterization.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit dataset/code availability statement and repository link in the abstract; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing hardware and training disclosures remain. Although Gemini-3-pro disappears from the introduction, Figure 3 still identifies it, so that implementation disclosure is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the Qwen2.5-VL technical report and Retrieving Any Relevant Moments, modestly extending attribution and temporal-grounding coverage. DeepSport is additionally discussed in the benchmark-comparison prose after already appearing in v1's table. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology edits, places benchmark formulation before data collection in Section 3.1, revises affiliations and adds acknowledgements. The main section structure and narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The same seven figures and six tables remain. v2 corrects Figure 6(b)'s axis labels, revises Figure 7(a)'s markers and scale, relabels and resizes Figure 5, expands captions and repositions several displays. Page margins and bibliography styling also change, without a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes verifiable reporting inconsistencies: the mIoU prose, swapped ICR/FLC chart labels and incorrect human-evaluation gain. Clearer captions and the new code/data access statement also improve usability. These are limited gains: the scientific contribution remains stable, revised scores are not explained, and referenced appendices remain absent from the supplied PDFs.
